newsitem.title: UK: IPE crude slips back, gas oil little changed.
newsitem.headline: IPE crude slips back, gas oil little changed.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures slipped back in quiet trade by the London midsession, as the market nervously awaited the New York open for direction, brokers said.
By 1158 GMT, front month crude was 22 cents lower at $18.72 a barrel, with August gas oil 25 cents higher on the day at $169.50 a tonne.
"The market's quite nervous ahead of the New York open," said one broker. "Most of the week's major moves have come out of the U.S."
The market was also keeping a close eye out for any further news from the U.N. concerning its awaited approval for Iraq's aid distribution plan, brokers said.
Crude came off sharply at the open, down over 20 cents, but traders said this was a correction from a late spurt of trade on Thursday.
Brent bounced back in late Thursday trade after the speculative dump of gasoline futures in New York ahead of the expiry of the unleaded gasoline August contract.
The United Nations said late on Thursday it expected Iraq's aid distribution plan to get the go-ahead early next week.
But some brokers believe the UN news is already factored into the market, and are not expecting the approval to spur any major moves.
A UN spokesman attributed the delay in the rubber stamping of Iraq's aid distribution plan to a computer virus affecting one of the diskettes containing Baghdad's proposals.
"It is settled from our point of view. We asked Iraq for certain assurances...and we received them in writing," the spokesman said.
